summary: Message reads guard the messages stream before anything writes to it: a subject in both stores lists once, a page is never empty with more to come, a cursor into the stream is refused by an older build rather than misread, a stream item's lifecycle step is checked and recorded atomically, and the shard's peer list is read once per member start (db break-up step 4c-1, part A)

replay.detail: Nothing new is written. A stream item's lifecycle step is now decided and recorded in one writer transaction on the shard.

rules.detail: A message subject that the graph holds as message.sent is the graph's: no message page, mailbox, delivery snapshot or conversation lists a stream item under it. A message page whose rows all fail its recipient or open check, which run after its query's limit, reads on, and its stream half fills what those rows left, so a page is empty only at the end. The shard's replication peers are read again only when a member starts or the members asked change.

compatibility.detail: GET /v1/messages/page cursors that point into the messages stream name the position in a new stream_after field and leave out after. Every earlier build, v0.3.25 included, needs after, so it answers such a cursor with invalid message cursor: the listing starts over. A build before the stream would otherwise read a stream position as a graph index past its end and end the listing early. This build still reads a v0.3.25 cursor that names a stream position in after. A member whose messages shard did not open answers a stream cursor with 410 cursor-gap, with full_resync, and the listing starts over. Cursors into the graph are unchanged.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores the earlier reads. A page cursor this build gave into the stream is refused by the earlier build, and the listing starts over.
